evidence: backend/servers/api-server/src/services/scheduler/mod.rs:666-680 — the announcement target-resolution helper's `"roles"` branch fans out via `SELECT DISTINCT om.user_id FROM organization_members om WHERE om.organization_id = $1 AND om.role_id = ANY($2) AND om.status = 'active'`, reading the LEGACY organization_members table (migration 00005).

The sibling `"all"` branch in the same match (mod.rs:584-598) was DELIBERATELY migrated off that table, with an in-code comment: 'membership lives in `user_memberships` (migration 00128, the canonical authz spine)' and joins `user_memberships` with revoked_at/expires_at freshness filters. The `"roles"` branch was not migrated and still trusts organization_members.

Migration 00128 (crates/db/migrations/00128_user_memberships.sql) declares user_memberships canonical and BACKFILLS from organization_members ('Backfill from `organization_members`. Map legacy role_type -> unified role') — i.e. organization_members is the legacy source, not the forward write path. If new/updated memberships are written only to user_memberships, role-targeted announcements will fan out to a stale audience and silently MISS residents whose active membership exists only in user_memberships (missed-notification correctness bug, not a style nit).

Schema divergence compounds it: announcement role targets are role_id UUIDs matched against organization_members.role_id, whereas user_memberships carries a `role VARCHAR(64)` enum and no role_id — so the fix is a real remodel (resolve role_id -> unified role, or dual-source), not a table rename. Landable backend-only investigation: confirm whether organization_members is still dual-written; if not, re-express the roles fanout against the canonical membership source. Reachable in production via publish_scheduled_announcements -> dispatch_announcement_notifications for any 'roles' target_type announcement.

backend/servers/api-server/src/services/auth.rs:97 — `rng.try_fill_bytes(&mut bytes).expect("OS rng failed")` inside `generate_token()` (email-verification / password-reset tokens); the fn returns `String`, so a CSPRNG failure panics the request thread instead of surfacing an error.

backend/servers/api-server/src/services/oauth.rs:918 — same pattern in `generate_random_b64()`, the single entropy source for OAuth authorization codes, access/refresh tokens, client ids AND client secrets (per its own doc-comment). A panic here aborts the OAuth token/registration request mid-flight.
backend/servers/api-server/src/services/totp.rs:153 — same `.expect("OS rng failed")` generating the AES-GCM nonce in `encrypt_secret()` on the MFA-enrollment path.

All three are per-request, security-critical, and infallible-signatured (`-> String`). OS getrandom failure is rare (fd exhaustion / broken /dev/urandom) but when it happens the response is a panic (dropped connection or 500 via catch-panic) rather than a clean 503/AuthError, and there is no test forcing the failure branch. Landable backend-only fix: change these helpers to return `Result<_, _>` and map the rng error to the existing error enums (AuthError / OAuth error / TotpError), or centralize on one fallible CSPRNG helper. Low-probability but auth-critical.

backend/servers/api-server/src/services/actions/delay.rs:54-60 — `DelayConfig::to_duration()` computes `Duration::from_secs(self.duration * 60|3600|86400)` where `self.duration: u64` is deserialized straight from user/workflow config (parse_config -> serde_json::from_value, no bound applied yet).

The MAX_DELAY_SECONDS (7 days) cap is only checked AFTER to_duration() runs (delay.rs:99-105: parse -> `to_duration()` -> then `if duration.as_secs() > MAX_DELAY_SECONDS`). So the multiplication happens on the still-unbounded value: a large `duration` with unit Days/Hours overflows the u64 multiply — panic in debug builds (arithmetic overflow), silent two's-complement wrap in release, which can even produce a small wrapped value that then passes the 7-day cap and schedules a wrong delay.

Reachable from workflow execution (Epic 94 delay action) with attacker/operator-controlled action config. Landable backend-only fix: validate `self.duration` against the max (or use `checked_mul` / `saturating_mul`) BEFORE constructing the Duration, so an out-of-range value is rejected with ConfigurationError instead of overflowing. Low severity (config-authoring path, not anonymous input) but a genuine unchecked-arithmetic-before-validation smell.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/lib/api.ts:213-221 — the hand-rolled axios response interceptor has an unauthorized branch `if (error.response?.status === 401 && onUnauthorizedCallback) { onUnauthorizedCallback(); }`. `onUnauthorizedCallback` is a module-level `let` (api.ts:180) set ONLY inside `createAxiosInstance` from `config.onUnauthorized` (api.ts:196).

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx:337 — the sole production caller wires the client with `configureApiClient({ getToken: getAccessToken })` and passes NO `onUnauthorized`. Therefore `onUnauthorizedCallback` is `undefined` at runtime and the 401 branch (api.ts:220) is dead code in production — a 401 neither logs the user out nor triggers a token refresh; the request just rejects with a transformed ApiError.

The gap has real consumers: frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/sentiment/hooks/useSentiment.ts:35+ and frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/predictive-maintenance/hooks/usePredictiveMaintenance.ts call `getApiClient()` directly, and their own header comments (useSentiment.ts:18-19, usePredictiveMaintenance.ts:9-10) advertise `401 -> onUnauthorized` as a benefit that never fires. When the access token expires, these production feature calls fail silently with an error instead of re-authenticating.

Impact / landable frontend-only fix: pass an `onUnauthorized` handler in the AuthContext.tsx:337 `configureApiClient({...})` call (e.g. invoke `logout()` or the queued `refreshToken()` + replay). Confidence medium: wiring is fully traced statically; net user impact depends on token TTL and whether the separate generated `@ppt/api-client` covers the main flows, so not upgraded to high.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx:449-462 — `refreshToken` implements a careful concurrency-safe silent-refresh: it de-duplicates concurrent callers via `isRefreshing`/`refreshPromise` refs so N parallel 401s coalesce into ONE `refreshTokenInternal()` round-trip. It is exposed on the context value (AuthContext.tsx:599 and dep array :610).

No production code path invokes it. A repo-wide grep for `refreshToken` consumers across apps/ppt-web/src returns only the definition, the context-value entries, and *.test.tsx files — no interceptor, hook, or component calls `useAuth().refreshToken()`. Combined with the dead `onUnauthorized` branch (see api-401 finding), ppt-web has NO 401 -> refresh -> retry pipeline for the hand-rolled `getApiClient()` client: an expired access token is never silently refreshed at request time.

So the queued-refresh machinery is effectively dead in production (exercised only by unit tests). Either it should be wired into the api.ts unauthorized branch (call `refreshToken()`, then replay the original request on success) or the runtime silent-refresh contract it implies is missing.

Impact: reliability/completeness gap on token expiry (low severity — sessions still work until the access token lapses, then the user hits errors/forced re-login instead of a transparent refresh). Landable frontend-only fix: connect `refreshToken()` to the 401 handler resolved by the api-401 finding above.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/lib/api.ts:321 — `export default getApiClient();` is evaluated at module-load time. `getApiClient()` lazily creates `apiInstance` via `createAxiosInstance()` with NO config, so the default export is permanently bound to an axios instance carrying the fallback `baseURL`/`timeout` (api.ts:63,68) and whatever the module-level getters were at import time.

Later, `configureApiClient(config)` (api.ts:298-300) REPLACES the module-level `apiInstance` with a brand-new `createAxiosInstance(config)` instance, and `resetApiClient()` (api.ts:307-311) sets it to null. Any importer of the `default` export keeps a reference to the ORIGINAL instance, which diverges from what `getApiClient()` returns afterward — a per-instance `baseURL`/`timeout` passed to `configureApiClient` would be silently ignored on the default-export instance (token injection happens to survive only because the getters are module-level `let`s read at request time).

Currently latent: no file imports the default (only named imports `{ configureApiClient, resetApiClient }` are used, AuthContext.tsx:39; lib/index.ts re-exports only named symbols). But it remains a footgun (a default export that is a stale, unconfigured singleton) plus an eager import-time side effect that constructs an axios instance nobody uses.

Impact: low — a trap for future callers, not an active bug. Landable frontend-only fix: drop the `export default getApiClient();` eager instantiation (prefer the explicit `getApiClient()` accessor), or make the default a lazy getter so it always resolves the current configured instance.

Multiple list handlers under backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/ take a user-controlled `limit` query param and forward it to the DB with only a default fill-in and NO upper-bound clamp: automation.rs:395 `.get_rule_logs_for_org(path.id, org_id, query.limit)` (limit: i32, default_limit at :156, no `.min()`), disputes.rs:928 `query.limit.unwrap_or(50)`, faults.rs:647, legal.rs:906, listings.rs:300 & :1050, building_certifications.rs:167 & :699, budgets.rs:61/86/107 (`limit: q.limit` passed straight through), community.rs:545/696/812.

The value reaches SQL LIMIT unclamped. Confirmed downstream: crates/db/src/repositories/automation.rs:324-355 `get_rule_logs_for_org` binds the caller's `limit` directly into `... ORDER BY started_at DESC LIMIT $2` (`.bind(limit)` at :348) with no clamp. So `GET ...?limit=2000000000` makes Postgres attempt to materialize up to ~2.1B rows -> unbounded memory/latency, a resource-exhaustion DoS on an authenticated but low-privilege endpoint.

Negative values are a second hazard on the same path: `limit: i32`/`Option<i64>` accepts `?limit=-1`, and Postgres rejects a negative LIMIT with an error, so the handler returns an unhandled 500 instead of a 400.

This is demonstrably an oversight, not a convention: sibling handlers in the SAME directory clamp correctly. buildings.rs:29-32 defines `DEFAULT_LIST_LIMIT=50` / `MAX_LIST_LIMIT=100` and applies `.unwrap_or(DEFAULT_LIST_LIMIT).min(MAX_LIST_LIMIT)` at :613-616; energy.rs, financial.rs, market_pricing.rs, meters.rs, operations.rs also clamp. The listed files simply omit the `.min(MAX)` step. Landable backend-only fix: clamp each `limit` to a shared MAX (and floor at >=0, or 400 on negative) before it reaches the repository, mirroring buildings.rs.

backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/financial.rs:561-571 (unit-ledger handler) matches on `state.financial_repo.get_account_with_transactions(account.id, 20).await` with only two arms: `Ok(Some(response)) => Ok(Json(response))` and a catch-all `_ => Ok(Json(FinancialAccountResponse { account, recent_transactions: vec![] }))`.

The `_ =>` arm collapses `Ok(None)` (legitimately empty) together with `Err(e)` (a real DB failure). A transient DB error therefore returns HTTP 200 with `recent_transactions: []` instead of surfacing a 500 -- the client is shown a financial account that appears to have zero recent transactions when in fact the fetch failed. On a money/ledger endpoint this is misleading financial data plus a swallowed error (no tracing on the error branch, so the failure is also invisible in logs).

Matches the reviewer pattern 'Axum handler that returns StatusCode::OK on an error branch'. Landable backend-only fix: split the arms so `Err(e)` maps to a 500 (with a `tracing::error!`) and only `Ok(None)` yields the empty-transactions fallback.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/ai-chat/hooks/useAiChat.ts:31-46 (apiFetch) and frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/meters/hooks/useOcrMeterReading.ts:26-35 (ocrFetch) issue requests with the native browser `fetch()` and set only `Content-Type` — they never attach an `the `Authorization` header (Bearer type) <token>` header. Since the api-server is Bearer-JWT based (no cookie session), these requests reach the backend with no credential and should be rejected with 401, breaking AI-chat and OCR for authenticated users. frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/ai-chat/hooks/useAiChat.ts:131-142 (useDeleteSession) calls `await fetch(\`${API_BASE}/sessions/${sessionId}\`, { method: 'DELETE' })` directly and never checks `response.ok`, unlike every other call in the file which routes through `apiFetch` (L31-46) that throws on a non-2xx status. frontend/apps/reality-web/src/app/[locale]/auth/callback/page.tsx:83-91 — the SSO callback pulls `error` and `error_description` off the query string with searchParams.get(...) and passes them straight into setError(errorDescription || errorParam), which then renders as

{error}

on line 131. There is no allow-list of expected error codes, no length cap, and no scrubbing.

React JSX escaping prevents HTML/JS injection so this is NOT XSS, but an attacker who can hand a victim a link to /<locale>/auth/callback?error=x&error_description=Please+call+1-800-... renders arbitrary attacker-controlled body text under our origin, with our SSO chrome and our real 'Return Home' button — a page-shaped phishing surface hosted from the real reality-web SSO callback URL. Because the URL is legitimately linked from OAuth error redirects, users are trained to trust content on that route.

Additionally the same file (162 lines) has zero next-intl usage on the 4-locale portal: 'Login Failed' (L130), 'Return Home' (L133), 'Loading...' (L66), 'Completing login...' (L144), and the constructed 'Invalid state token. Please try logging in again.' (L106) all render English regardless of locale.

Fix vector: constrain error to a known enum ('access_denied', 'invalid_state', 'server_error', ...) and translate via useTranslations('auth.sso.error.<code>'); fall back to a single generic key when the code is unknown. Drop the raw error_description from the rendered UI (log it only). Wrap the remaining strings in t().

mobile-native/shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/three/two/bit/ppt/reality/util/FormatUtils.kt:18-24 — FormatUtils.formatPrice(price: Long, currency) documents '@param price The price in minor units (e.g., cents)', but the actual system contract is whole-currency units, so the docstring directly contradicts every real caller and the wire format.

The wire deserializer is explicit that prices are whole units: api/DecimalStringSerializers.kt:37-49 DecimalAsLongSerializer does `raw.substringBefore('.').toLong()` and its own doc says 'Prices in the portal models are whole-currency Longs, so the sub-unit scale carried by DECIMAL(15,2) is dropped' ('200000.00' -> 200000). listing/ListingModels.kt:96,123 declare `val price: Long` fed by that serializer.

All 10 production call sites pass the whole-unit `listing.price` (e.g. androidApp .../ui/listing/ListingHeaderSection.kt:55, ui/home/HomeScreen.kt:457,676, ui/search/SearchScreen.kt:1060, ui/favorites/FavoritesScreen.kt:551,625, ui/listing/ListingPriceHistory.kt:70,76,97). formatPriceAmount() also hard-codes whole-unit thresholds — `price >= 1_000_000` renders '1.00M' meaning one million currency units, not one million cents.

Impact: any future caller (or iOS port) that trusts the 'minor units / cents' docstring and passes cents will render prices 100x too large AND cross the M/K abbreviation thresholds 100x early. This is a latent money-formatting contract defect, not a style nit. Landable mobile-only fix: correct the KDoc to 'whole-currency units (sub-unit scale already dropped by DecimalAsLongSerializer)', matching the serializer's own wording.

mobile-native/shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/three/two/bit/ppt/reality/auth/SsoInitiation.kt:buildUrl — `fun buildUrl(state: String): String = "$PM_APP_SCHEME://sso?callback=$CALLBACK&state=$state"` splices CALLBACK (= 'reality://sso', containing ':' and '//') into a query-parameter VALUE with no percent-encoding, and does not encode `state` either.

This is the asymmetric mirror of the inbound path, which is careful: navigation/DeepLinkRouter.kt.urlDecode form-url-DEcodes every query component and its KDoc records a previously-shipped encode/decode parity bug ('The shared router previously returned the raw, still-encoded substring ... breaking SSO validation on iOS'). The outbound leg has no matching encode step.

Currently non-exploitable because CALLBACK is a fixed constant with no '&' or extra '=' and the minted `state` nonce is 64-char hex (URL-safe) — but it is brittle: the moment the callback or state carries a reserved character ('&', '=', a query of its own) the PM app's query parser will mis-split the URL. Landable mobile-only fix: percent-encode the callback and state values (e.g. Ktor `encodeURLParameter()` / `encodeURLQueryComponent()`) in buildUrl, symmetric with DeepLinkRouter's decode. Covered by the existing SsoInitiationTest surface.
